description: An end-use technology that consumes electricity and can be built, such as a hydrogen electrolyzer, direct air capture, or an industrial heat pump. Its consumption is a decision, valued by what it produces: `technology_efficiency` converts electricity into product and `price_per_unit` prices the product. It carries the capital and operating cost of new capacity together with its capacity limits, minimum consumption, and ramp limits.

available.description: Indicator of whether the component is connected and online (`true`) or disconnected, offline, or down (`false`).

power_systems_type.description: Corresponding type to be used in PCM modeling.

region.description: Location where the component applies. Can be a zone or node.

capacity_limits.description: Minimum and maximum allowable installed capacity for a technology. Units: MW.

unit_size.description: Used for discrete investment decisions. Size of each unit being built. Units: MW.

capital_costs.description: Capital and interconnection cost for investing in a technology (capital cost in USD/MW).

operation_costs.description: Fixed and variable O&M costs, the variable cost per MWh consumed. Units: USD/MWh.

min_power.description: Minimum consumption as a fraction of installed capacity. Units: 1.

ramp_limits.description: Maximum decrease and increase in consumption between operation periods. Units: MW/min.

technology_efficiency.description: Electricity consumed per unit of product. Ex: MWh per tonne of hydrogen for electrolyzers. Units: 1.

price_per_unit.description: Price or value per unit of product. Ex: USD per tonne of hydrogen for electrolyzers. Units: USD/t.

lifetime.description: Maximum number of years a technology can be active once installed. Units: yr.

financial_data.description: Struct containing relevant financial information for a technology.

title: DemandSideTechnology
